title: New JavaScript obfuscation technique: Formatting a script can turn it into a different program
description: A new JavaScript obfuscation technique has been demonstrated where formatting changes to a script can transform it into a completely different program. This technique leverages 186 different methods to alter script behavior through formatting, which can be tested via provided online tools and demos. The technique is primarily a research and development insight into JavaScript code manipulation rather than a direct vulnerability or exploit in existing software.

aiSummary: This security news reports on a novel JavaScript obfuscation approach where applying formatting, minification, or deobfuscation processes to a script can cause it to execute as a different program. The technique involves 186 distinct methods to achieve this divergence, allowing a single script to morph into multiple behaviors depending on how it is processed. Demonstrations and technical breakdowns are available on the referenced websites, illustrating the concept and its implications for code analysis and security tooling.
aiImpact: The impact is primarily on code analysis, reverse engineering, and security tooling that rely on formatting or deobfuscation to understand JavaScript code. This technique can potentially evade detection or cause misinterpretation of script behavior by automated tools. However, there is no direct evidence of active exploitation or vulnerabilities in software products. The technique may complicate threat detection and forensic analysis but does not itself constitute a software vulnerability.
